A former NSW Liberal politician is facing the possibility of a significant jail term after a jury found him guilty of raping a 13-year-old boy.

The former MP Rory Amon was found guilty by a jury, after about four hours of deliberation on Friday, of one count of sexual intercourse with a person aged between 10 and 14 and indecently assaulting a child.

The 37-year-old was facing his second NSW supreme court trial after a different jury acquitted him in March on eight separate charges of child sexual offending, but could not reach a verdict on the two counts decided on Friday.

The charges related to Amon’s interactions with a 13-year-old boy who the former MP met on an adults-only website, the court heard.

Amon always maintained his innocence, saying he held an honest and reasonable belief that the boy was over the age of 16.

The original trial was told the boy inflated his age when signing up to the gay hook-up app, and again while talking with Amon.

Amon and the boy exchanged explicit images before a 2017 meeting in the carpark of the boy’s apartment block, the court heard.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at the time he first contacted the youth, amon was working full-time for the federal mp for mackellar, jason falinski. Amon went on to serve two terms on Northern Beaches council before being elected as the Liberal MP for the state seat of Pittwater in 2023.

The charges scuppered Amon’s fledgling career in state politics, forcing his expulsion from the Liberal party and his resignation after his election in March 2023.

His exit had implications for the state Liberals, which lost the formerly safe seat to a teal independent at the subsequent byelection.

Amon remains on bail and will return to court for a sentencing hearing on 27 November.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he is the third former nsw mp convicted of sexual offences in recent years. The former Kiama MP and Coalition minister Gareth Ward was jailed in 2025 for the sexual abuse of two young men, including a political staffer who was intoxicated after an event at NSW Parliament House. His three-year-nine-month minimum term expires in April 2029.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the former nsw minister milton orkopoulos was found guilty in 2023 of sexually abusing teenage boys while he was a state labor mp. A jury found the 65-year-old guilty of 26 charges of sexual offending against four underage boys and supplying them with drugs over a decade, ending in 2003.

He had already served more than a decade in prison for sexual assault of a minor, indecent assault, supplying heroin and cannabis and other offences.

When the outbreak was first detected in May, it resembled a single, giant blaze, with infections concentrated in a handful of towns in one province.

Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's artificial intelligence software Copilot, have been affected by "connectivity problems".

Customers are reporting varying levels of access - many have not been able to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps.

Some users have been able to use Teams and are using messaging and online meeting functions without issues.

More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps according to Microsoft's website.

The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed, but monitoring website Downdetector had 140,000 people from 74 countries report issues with Outlook on Thursday evening.

The real figure affected is likely much higher because Downdetector relies primarily on users self-reporting.

Microsoft 365 is also used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services.

Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic have both reported problems as a result of the outage.

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which has caused some tools to not work as expected.

From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies, disruption across the globe has been widespread.

Courts from Los Angeles to Texas warned that communications might be delayed.

In Canada, the public broadcaster CBC reported that a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto was experiencing email issues, but that patient care was not affected.

The government of Japan also said its shared IT platform had been disrupted.

Across the UK, GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools have been affected by the outage.

Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains, while several large police forces are urging members of the public to call if they want to make a report.

Microsoft has ruled out a cyber-attack and attributed the ongoing outage to "elevated load" on its infrastructure.

The term refers to when servers are handling a much higher volume of stress than they usually do.

In the case of the Microsoft outage, a large number of servers became "unexpectedly unavailable", the company said, which sent added traffic to remaining servers, straining these.

On Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe and improvement in North America.

The company added it is focused on "addressing the remaining areas of disruption" and warned "some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue".

In an earlier statement, the tech giant had said that its attempted fixes were "not taking as expected".

Although email service Outlook appears to be resuming for some, the outage has so far lasted for more than 20 hours - in outage terms that is considered a long time.

Prof James Ferryman from the University of Reading's department of computer science said the details the company has disclosed provide some clues.

"What Microsoft has told us is that the part of its servers that sets up secure connections is getting swamped, and once that happens the server just stops answering," he said.

"The trouble is that this kind of failure snowballs.

"One server falls over, its work gets passed to the next one, and meanwhile huge numbers of phones and laptops keep trying to get back in.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "you can't just turn it all back on at once. You have to bring it back bit by bit. ".

The challenge is therefore not just fixing the fault, but managing the huge surge of devices trying to reconnect once services start coming back online.

Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the "most disruptive" business email outage "of all time".

He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he "cannot recall" an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal.

Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences.

"Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is.

"Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said.

#373. Study Hard, Get a Career and Get Ahead? It’s Not What It Used to Be.

📅 13 Nov 2026

Study Hard, Get a Career and Get Ahead? It’s Not What It Used to Be.

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/world/europe/education-meritocracy.html

From India to France, the implicit meritocratic bargain that underwrote stable societies by providing advancement to new generations is breaking down.

Diungkapkan bahwa protest movements have long relied on students as some of the most ardent foot soldiers. Young people have been on the front lines of protests against war, climate change and racial inequality. But in huge protests that have shaken India and France this fall, students have revolted against the failed promises of education itself.

Diungkapkan bahwa in india, students took to the streets after the government abruptly canceled the results of a medical-school admissions exam because test questions had been leaked online. Aspiring doctors had to take the test again, after many spent years studying for up to 12 hours a day in hopes of winning one of the coveted spots — and the chance of upward mobility. Young people across the country saw the scandal as emblematic of a broken education system and were furious.

Diungkapkan bahwa in france, students in poor suburbs outside paris began protesting the decrepit physical condition of their schools, an opaque university admissions system and absent teachers. French education had long promised to serve as a “social elevator” enabling young people to advance in society, but had fallen into disrepair. Soon, demonstrations spread across the country and, in some cities, spiraled into rioting.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in both countries, the anger of the students shows no signs of abating. And while in many ways France and India could hardly be more different, their unrest was sparked by a similar source of outrage: the breakdown of a foundational social contract that one could call the meritocratic bargain.

Berdasarkan laporan, it is a promise that lies at the core of many countries’ political compacts. Educational achievements are a good measure of merit because education is open to all and leads to valuable skills. Though specifics can vary, the central proposition usually goes something like this: A fair society rewards merit. Therefore, education should be a route to social and economic advancement.

Diungkapkan bahwa the value of this system is not just that it selects for those with high ability, but also that it offers a justification for the resulting socioeconomic hierarchy — including who ends up at the bottom. “All selection mechanisms generate losers,” said Nicholas Kuipers, a professor at Princeton University who studies the politics of meritocracy. “The question is, Who do you want to be a loser, and who do you want to be a winner?”.

Diungkapkan bahwa a bird that flies south from its breeding grounds in siberia to winter in south and south-east asia has been found thousands of miles off course in cumbria. Regrettably, it was found by a cat.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, chris hind, cumbria’s county recorder for birds, said it was “extraordinary” that a siberian rubythroat was found on his patch, albeit dead. There have been only 17 recorded instances of the bird in the UK, 15 of those in the northern Scottish isles.

Diungkapkan bahwa hind was contacted by the rspb at the weekend after a womanwho lives in a remote north cumbrian valley reported the bird. She had recognised it was out of the ordinary and put the dead bird in her freezer.

Diungkapkan bahwa “she realised that it was something unusual,” hind said. “She probably didn’t realise how incredibly unusual it is. There are only two accepted records of it from mainland Britain. ”.

The woman, who wants to remain anonymous, told the BBC she had “heard the cat flap go” and her heart sank when her cat “brought her a bird and trotted off”.

“I saw the bird’s distinctive, beautiful orange-red feather patch under its beak but I couldn’t recognise the species,” she said.

Quite why the bird appears to have headed west, rather than south, is a mystery although Hind pointed to the puzzle of yellow-browed warblers that have been spotted in the UK in increasing numbers in recent decades.

“It used to be thought that these are birds which had just got lost but there are academics now thinking that it may be something rather more purposeful,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hind said the bird brought in by the cat was very underweight, weighing 28 grams (just under 1oz). Textbooks say it should be about 73 grams.

Diungkapkan bahwa siberian rubythroats were also extremely secretive, he said. “They tend to creep around in the vegetation and the place where it was found was a place hugely vegetated, lots of trees, lots of bushes, lots of hedges in a remote little valley. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the plan is now for academics to take samples and then the bird – currently in hind’s freezer – will go to tullie house museum in carlisle. The nuclear agency has not been able to inspect any sites attacked by the US and Israel last year.

The UN's nuclear watchdog has said it is "increasingly concerned" about a nuclear facility in Iran which it has not been allowed to inspect.

Berdasarkan laporan, iran informed the international atomic energy agency (iaea) of plans to set up the uranium enrichment plant in the city of isfahan a day before israel began attacking its nuclear sites last june. The US joined the strikes later that month.

In a report seen by news agencies, the IAEA said it does not know the exact location or whether it contains nuclear material.

Since the start of the latest war, Iran has restricted IAEA inspectors' access to its nuclear sites, preventing the agency from verifying its enriched uranium stockpile.

Sebagaimana diketahui, under a 2015 nuclear deal, iran agreed to limit its enriched uranium stockpile to 300kg and enrichment to 3. 67% purity. It subsequently exceeded both.

Before the June 2025 strikes, it had accumulated an estimated 441kg enriched to 60%, close to weapons grade.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the nuclear complex at isfahan suffered extensive damage in us and israeli strikes, particularly the parts above the ground. The condition of its underground facilities is not clear.

The IAEA believes much of Iran's highly enriched uranium was stored there.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the agency's lack of information about [iran's] nuclear material and access to facilities to verify it is a matter of serious proliferation concern. and needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency," it said in the latest report.

Iran announced plans for the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP) on 12 June 2025, shortly after an IAEA resolution which declared Iran had failed to meet its nuclear safeguards obligations.

Iran initially agreed to allow inspectors to visit the facility, but the inspection was cancelled after Israel launched attacks the following day.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the iaea's latest calls come almost a year after it made a similar appeal to iran. At the time it said it had only inspected some of the 13 nuclear facilities that were "unaffected" by the attacks and none of the seven that were.

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmvg2dvw0355o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

All parties have been banned at the university.

Four Nigerian students have died after attending a party in the south-eastern town of Nsukka to celebrate the end of their final exams.

The cause of death has not been confirmed but police spokesman Daniel Ndukwe said the two men and two women had reportedly fallen ill after consuming alcoholic drinks at the party.

The University of Nigeria Nsukka has declared three days of mourning, during which academic and social activities will be suspended.

The tragedy comes amid a wider crackdown on fake and adulterated alcoholic drinks in Nigeria, where the food and drug regulator has been raiding suspected producers of unsafe food and beverages.

The university's Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simon Ortuanya, said the university had received a distress call at 22:00 on Wednesday, and sent security personnel to a house party at Praise Lodge, outside the campus in Nsukka's Hilltop area.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the preliminary investigation and interim report point to alleged alcohol abuse or drug paraphernalia and things like that. But we are not conclusive on those matters," he said.

He described the deaths as "tragic and painful".

"As a community, we mourn, not just alone, we mourn with the families, the parents that have suffered these years to train the men and women in their studies," he said.

Ortuanya also announced a ban on signing-out celebrations, which are commonly held by final-year students to mark the completion of their studies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the celebrations often involve parties, dancing, photographs and friends signing one another's shirts. He urged students to use graduation as a time to reflect on their university experience and prepare for life beyond campus.

The university said it was working with security agencies to establish what had caused the deaths.

Diungkapkan bahwa the police have also launched an investigation. They said alcoholic drinks had been recovered from the scene and the bodies taken to a mortuary for autopsies.

The investigation comes amid wider concerns about unsafe alcoholic drinks in Nigeria.

In September, dozens of people fell ill after consuming locally made alcoholic drinks and herbal mixtures in communities across Ondo State, south-west Nigeria.

More than 11 people died in the Araromi-Obu area, while more than 50 others were hospitalised.

Investigations found that some of the drinks had been contaminated with methanol, a highly toxic form of alcohol that can cause blindness and death.

Diungkapkan bahwa nigeria's food and drug regulator, nafdac, reported more than 150 cases, including 48 confirmed deaths. More than 80 people were hospitalised, and five lost their sight.

The regulator has been carrying out raids across the country, targeting facilities suspected of producing fake or adulterated alcoholic drinks, food and beverages.

Nigeria has long struggled with the sale of unsafe and adulterated products, which campaigners warn pose a serious threat to public health.

Singer, 76, was in Manchester with his band for penultimate UK show of his Songs in the Key of Life anniversary tour.

When Stevie Wonder’s team just called to say: “Can we all come to your restaurant in Stalybridge at 11pm on a Sunday?” Ryan Robinson, of course, said yes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, first the band turned up, and then – at 12. 30am – the man himself arrived. Hours later, staff at the Cafe Continental were sharing a £1,000 tip.

It was, the co-owner admitted, “all a bit mad”, as he praised Wonder as someone who was happy to chat to everybody, and the team around him as down to earth and extremely polite.

Wonder, 76, was in Manchester with his band for the Sunday night gig at Co-op Live on his Songs in the Key of Life 50th anniversary tour.

It was the penultimate night of a 13-date European leg of the tour in which Wonder performed all 21 songs from his most celebrated album, which includes Have a Talk With God, Sir Duke, Joy Inside My Tears and Isn’t She Lovely.

Robinson told the Manchester Evening News that some of the musicians on the tour had already been in a few times, “as they often tour with other artists”.

“Every time they’ve visited, they’ve been like: ‘Stevie might come’, and we were always just thinking that it would be amazing but we never expected anything from it.

Berdasarkan laporan, “his band visited again on saturday and then we got the call to say they wanted to come again with stevie’s youngest daughter after their show in manchester, and they said again that stevie might come. We stayed open late for them, and then he turned up – it was all a bit mad!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we normally just do a roast service on sunday, so it was a bit of a scramble to make it all happen and ensure we had the full menu ready for them, but everybody was so lovely. Stevie is actually a really nice guy and was happy to pose for photographs and have a chat. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, among the late-night diners was wonder’s daughter aisha, for whom he wrote isn’t she lovely when she was a newborn. You wouldn’t think they were these massive global superstars. Robinson said: “His daughter, his family, and his entire team are just all down to earth and very polite. I just kept looking over being like: ‘Is this actually happening?’ We’ve still not come to terms with it now!”.

Cafe Continental describes itself as a neighbourhood restaurant in the heart of Stalybridge, “offering a modern, day to night dining experience”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the superstar and his musicians dined on steak and seafood and before leaving they gave a £1,000 tip, which was shared among staff, robinson said. After the visit the restaurant posted on Facebook: “Surreal things happen now and again. This is one of them! Pleasure to welcome Mr Stevie Wonder to the restaurant to close off his tour!”.

Berdasarkan laporan, robinson said he thought the band had found the restaurant on social media. “But it’s brought them out here into the suburbs and it’s really nice to see. “If it wasn’t for social media, they more than likely may have Googled something nearby and it might have led them to the city centre,” he told the BBC. “It’s good for the area. For a small independent business like us to receive so much traction from this … getting a major celebrity to this town itself, it does a lot. ”.

#387. UK’s biggest insurer hit by rise in subsidence claims after record hot summer

UK’s biggest insurer hit by rise in subsidence claims after record hot summer

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/13/uk-insurer-rise-in-subsidence-claims-aviva-hastings-direct-axa

Increase reported by Aviva after Hastings Direct said claims were up 140% in August and Axa said it had been a ‘surge year’.

The UK’s largest insurer has been hit by a rise in subsidence claims after an extremely hot summer left households across the country grappling with the fallout from the growing climate crisis.

Aviva said on Friday it had experienced the jump amid an industry-wide surge in households filing subsidence claims with their insurers to cover repairs, which typically are needed to address cracks, sloping floors, and off-kilter doors and windows.

Berdasarkan laporan, it follows two record hot summers in the uk; august this year was the joint hottest month ever recorded around the world. Drier summers cause the ground under houses to shrink, which undermines a property’s foundations. It then expands in wetter winters, which can further damage homes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, aviva experienced a “peak subsidence period” between july and september, with claims continuing into october, its chief executive, amanda blanc, told bloomberg in an interview on friday. Aviva would not provide any further detail on the scale of the increase in claims.

Diungkapkan bahwa blanc said homeowners could reduce the risk of subsidence by keeping a close eye on drains, pipes and gutters, and fixing any leaks that could affect the ground under homes. “It’s about managing trees and plumbing,” she said.

Diungkapkan bahwa a number of fellow insurers have also experienced a rise in claims in recent months. Hastings Direct said it received record subsidence claims in August, up 140% compared with a year earlier. Axa, one of the UK’s biggest home insurers, has said it has been a “surge year” for subsidence.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the value of claims have also hit a record high. The average subsidence claim in the UK hit a high of £20,000 between April and June, more than £2,000 higher than a year earlier, according to the Association of British Insurers. Insurers paid out £72m for domestic subsidence claims, compared with £60m in the same period last year.

Berdasarkan laporan, millions of homes are at risk of subsidence because of the worsening climate crisis, according to the british geological survey, which estimates that up to 11% of uk homes – more than 4. 2m houses – could be at risk by 2070. Older properties with shallow foundations and those built on clay-rich soil are facing the biggest threat, with areas including London, Essex, Kent and areas around Oxford among the most vulnerable.

Berdasarkan laporan, but despite the rise in subsidence claims, blanc said aviva was in rude health, having reported a 19% rise in general insurance premiums to £11. 8bn in the third quarter.

Berdasarkan laporan, “aviva is in great shape,” she said in a statement released alongside the company’s financial results. We continue to deliver strong, profitable growth, particularly in the capital-light areas of general insurance and wealth. “Our performance has been excellent in the first nine months of 2026, demonstrating once again the benefits of scale across our diversified business. ”.

In conversations with both American and Mexican officials over the last several months, Stephen Miller has insisted that illegal border crossings must be reduced, according to officials in both countries familiar with the private conversations but not authorized to discuss them.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the main forums for mr. ambassador to Mexico, Ronald ​Johnson, some of the officials said. Miller’s demands has been his near daily calls with the U. On calls with staff, Mr. S. Miller, previously the deputy chief of staff, frequently rails about the number of border crossings, despite their low figures, the officials said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that has been especially true in recent months, they said, as border crossings increased slightly, to the highest point in mr. Trump’s second term.

Note: Includes encounters outside official border crossings.

#391. How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House

📅 13 Nov 2026

How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c67429m3vem3o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

How could the Nvidia CEOâs affair threaten US national security?.

How close is Donald Trump to Jensen Huang?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the us president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, jensen huang wasn't just another tech billionaire seeking the president's ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America's most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nvidia makes the chips that power the ai revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities.

Berdasarkan laporan, but enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, jensen huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. Trump appeared sympathetic to this view, allowing Nvidia to resume sales of certain chips to China last year in return for a share of the revenue, although its most advanced Blackwell chips remain off limits.

But that relationship now looks rather more complicated.

The allegations surrounding Jensen Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, of no relation but a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, have raised the possibility that a foreign intelligence operation was targeting not just a powerful businessman, but someone with unusually close access to the American president.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, us intelligence reportedly suspects alice huang of having links to chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the allegations. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. But the affair has opened up a much bigger question: what did the administration in Washington know, and what did it do about it?.

That question leads directly to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, his department was responsible for controlling exports of sensitive american technology. It was also being pressed to act on concerns about Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China.

Berdasarkan laporan, on thursday, megaspeed chief executive, tan yong pong, also known as james tan, said the company "takes its compliance obligations under us export control laws extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the us government". He said the company had co-operated with US Commerce Department inspections.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a highly classified memo was shared with lutnick about the concerns surrounding alice huang and megaspeed. He resisted taking action against the company, a decision that is now under scrutiny.

Sebagaimana diketahui, other senior officials wanted a tougher response. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was among those who reportedly questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Commerce Department's blacklist.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there were also questions about why an investigation into the singapore-based company was stopped after nvidia intervened. The New York Times reported that Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce Department investigators probing suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed invoking a senior Trump appointee. The department allegedly then froze its investigation and handed the case to the Justice Department.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this apparently highlighted a significant disagreement about the direction of trump's china policy. Huang wanted access to the Chinese market. Other officials were supposedly worried about the national security consequences. Lutnick was caught in the middle.

Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy.

The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, members of congress from both parties want answers. Democrats have launched an investigation into how the Commerce Department vetted Chinese companies approved to buy AI chips. Republicans are also questioning the administration's approach.

And Jensen Huang's departure has not eased the pressure.

Republican representative John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on China, said it was in the national interest for Nvidia and other American AI firms to succeed, but that companies "should never jeopardise our nation's security" by giving Chinese firms access to their most advanced chips.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said Huang's resignation did not absolve him of responsibility, and urged Lutnick to explain why export control loopholes remain open.

Meanwhile Jensen Huang's team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he plans to cooperate with their request to testify behind closed doors.

The White House has not responded to the BBC's request for comment.

It has, however, told the New York Post that Trump has complete confidence in Lutnick, describing him as "the most transformative commerce secretary in modern history".

That is a fairly emphatic show of support, particularly amid reports that officials are weighing whether Lutnick should be forced out.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there are some obvious questions. If Lutnick had indeed been warned about the risks, why did his department fail to act? And if other senior officials were indeed pressing for action, why did it take so long?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the bbc has contacted the commerce department for comment. But there is an even bigger question for Trump.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the president cultivated a close relationship with huang. He was directly involved in decisions about chip sales to China. And, according to reporting in the New York Times, he was briefed on the intelligence concerns.

This is becoming difficult to dismiss as the misjudgement of one businessman or one government department.

Diungkapkan bahwa jensen huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the white house itself. How much influence did he have? What did the president know? And who was ultimately responsible for protecting America's most sensitive technology?.

Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently?.

#394. Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'

Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6702z750zvyo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Pat Cummins spent over an hour fielding questions over sandpapergate on Friday.

As Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins spent more than an hour being grilled by reporters over one of sport's biggest cheating scandals, the tension in the hall was occasionally pierced by muffled cheers.

Diungkapkan bahwa outside, a crucial match in the top tier of domestic cricket was getting under way. Cummins was clear he'd rather we all be talking about that.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but inside the nets at cricket central in sydney, he faced more than a dozen tv cameras and a gaggle of journalists several times as large. His goal: to put rumours of his involvement in "sandpapergate" to rest.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "i don't want to talk about this again after today," he said. "Even if it takes all day. I'll stay here until we have no more questions. ".

A book by his friend and former teammate Usman Khawaja has renewed scrutiny on a 2018 plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's third Test match against South Africa in Cape Town.

Three players admitted they were involved at the time and were handed lengthy bans, but in a memoir released last week, Khawaja said the entire Australian team knew about the sandpaper scheme.

His claims have plunged the Australian cricket world into chaos, thrown speculation over key figures from that Test - including star bowler Cummins who has since risen to hold what many joke is Australia's most important job - and reopened wounds for fans.

Sebagaimana diketahui, josh, 28, told the bbc he thought everyone had moved on: "it's just a bit crazy that it's all blown up again. I think it is a bit ridiculous, after eight years. ".

"I'm a bit bored of it," another spectator at the New South Wales vs South Australia Sheffield Shield match said.

Josh says he was surprised the scandal is back in the news.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, among fans, there's frustration that khawaja has chosen to come forward now, almost a decade on and at the start of an exciting summer, and year, of cricket. Though there's an argument there'd never be a good time for Khawaja, who retired from international cricket in January, to make these allegations.

There's worry about the impact on the men's team's performance this summer, after a lacklustre showing in South Africa last month - its first Test matches there since the 2018 incident.

And there's a sense of injustice that Australia can't seem to escape the scandal, given - according to many players themselves - how common boundary-bending on ball tampering apparently was in that era.

"It's a bit of a stitch up," 21-year-old James said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "every country has done it. if it wasn't us, it was probably going to be someone else. ".

Khawaja has said he owed it to the three players punished to tell his side of the story.

Khawaja's memoir is also causing rancour among current and former players and coaches.

In it, he said he had wanted the team to take collective responsibility for the tampering after batsman Cameron Bancroft was caught with the sandpaper on field.

Diungkapkan bahwa "i said: 'take this as a team. We knew what was going on, and we have to take it as a team'. We did this as a team. ".

However Khawaja has since said he didn't want to start a "witch hunt" and has refused to answer questions on exactly who he claims knew of the scheme, and what they knew.

David Warner, who received the most severe punishment of the Cape Town trio, said Khawaja had written the truth and that Cummins' press conference denying the claims "threw him under the bus".

Diungkapkan bahwa steve smith, the captain at the time who was also suspended, has been travelling overseas and is yet to say anything publicly about the claims in the book. Bancroft is also staying silent for now despite previously suggesting the bowlers knew.

But half of Australia's living cricket royalty and a slew of former coaches - some of whom have been accused of wrongdoing too - have thrown in their two cents.

And Cricket Australia is under pressure from some to reopen its investigation into sandpapergate - something chief executive Todd Greenberg has already ruled out.

Prof David Rowe of the University of Western Sydney told the BBC the saga was still so painful for many players and fans as the country sees itself as "a nation of good sports".

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the idea of being a good sport is two things. One is being good at sport, so you actually win. But the other side is that you do it honourably and fairly," he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, "many australians would see themselves as above all that. not the nation of good sports. That is: cheating is what other teams get up to. ".

He said the revelation was a "nasty shock" which brought the country "collective shame" which lingers today.

He says he doubts that the cricket scene would be able to move on without a fresh response from the governing body, Cricket Australia.

"One of the best ways to fuel conspiracy theories and keep sandpapergate going is to essentially say 'there's no more to see here' - especially when that comes from the authorities," Rowe said.

Australia kicked off it's summer with an ODI against England on Friday.

Asked about a fresh investigation, Cummins said it was a matter for Cricket Australia.

Over the marathon press conference - which one reporter suggested was the longest in Australian sporting history - Cummins was cautious, pausing often to consider his responses and to make sure they answered the questions being asked of him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but he was also frank - using strong words to reject what he said were "vague" claims by khawaja and admitting he was frustrated a friend had put him in this position. That's something I've been grappling with the last couple of days. "Friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, as the reporters ran out of steam, cummins said it was "annoying" that sandpapergate scandal was still a distraction for australian cricket. He gestured outside to the Sheffield Shield match and mentioned Friday's one-day international against England in Perth, from which he and other key players are being rested.

Berdasarkan laporan, "it's been eight years. Hopefully today we put a line through it and we're done and we can all move on to much more fun topics, like actual cricket. ".

"It's going to be hard to move on, given that there's two sides of the story and it doesn't look like either side is going to back down," James said.

'Wrong' and 'nonsense' - Cummins on Khawaja claims.

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/13/reselling-apps-dark-side-under-16s-social-media-ban-child-protection

Ministers consider banning under-16s from online marketplaces amid reported misuse of messaging functions and users’ photos.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in june, hannah* listed her seven-year-old daughter’s pink swimming costume for sale on vinted, hoping other parents surfing the reselling site would snap up the £1 offer. Her inbox pinged.

“So a little girl wore this yh [yeah]?” wrote a user with a male handle.

Berdasarkan laporan, after sending back a barbed “what do you think?”, hannah swiftly blocked the user and reported the incident to vinted. She described the exchange as “disgusting” and “disturbing”.

Her experience is just one of the many innocuous listings of children and young people’s secondhand clothes on reselling apps that are attracting sexualised comments through their direct messaging function.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the children’s society has said some young users of resale sites are increasingly being asked for indecent photos in exchange for money or gifts. Some photos of young users posted on the platforms have been AI deepfaked into nudes without their consent.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in response, ministers are considering banning under-16s from platforms such as depop, ebay and facebook marketplace, according to the sunday times, over mounting fears that their private messaging functions are the latest frontline in child exploitation. Vinted, which has a minimum age of 18, would have to join the other sites in gating access with strict age verification features.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the culture secretary, lisa nandy, said on sunday that the government was “looking seriously” at expanding the under-16s social media ban to include online marketplaces. It is understood the regulations were sent for cabinet signoff this week, with Nandy expected to present them to parliament in December.

Berdasarkan laporan, young women have posted on tiktok and reddit about their concerning interactions with buyers. Those exchanges include asking the seller if the item will come with used underwear if they buy it, or unsolicited sexual comments about their appearance.

Diungkapkan bahwa lucy* started reselling her pre-loved clothes on depop when she was 15 and has been subject to many unsettling experiences. “That made me feel like, oh my God, awful. Once, she listed an item of clothing for about £10 and a user requested to raise the price. “The person had changed it to £30 and said: ‘If you include your pants I’ll pay more’,” she said. ”.

She then discovered that images of her taken when she was under the age of 18, posted to advertise her clothes, had been scraped from Depop and were circulating on Reddit.

Diungkapkan bahwa “these pictures are actually still being resurfaced on these reddit pages, which is quite frustrating,” she said. “It would be me at 17 trying to sell a bikini, and these men have screenshotted these images … It’s not just me, it’s hundreds of other girls. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, about two years ago, lucy came across another social media platform, discord, where she found users had stolen her old vinted and depop photos and manipulated them using ai to make deepfakes of her “fully nude”. She said: “It’s deplorable that people think it’s acceptable to take people’s images and make them into AI porn – I felt really, really upset. ”.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

Diungkapkan bahwa vinted says minors can only access the site under the supervision of adult account holders, while depop says users must be aged 13 or over to set up an account, and over 18 to use paypal and the depop payment systems. However, the UK communications watchdog, Ofcom, has found that 15% of eight to 14-year-olds use Vinted each month, while another report has suggested that some children are able to bypass checks and access age-restricted online services.

Diungkapkan bahwa some child safety campaigners have expressed fears a sweeping social media ban could exclude children from the internet entirely. Karen Garland, the head of policy at the Marie Collins Foundation, a charity that supports victims of technology-assisted child sexual exploitation, said: “We need to make spaces for children and young people that are safer by design. And so, in some ways, extending a ban into other spaces may not be the best route overall. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa despite her experience, lucy is conflicted about the ban. “It’s a real shame because there are probably very young girls that maybe are from different backgrounds … that maybe really need that money. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, she acknowledged that there could be “extremely dangerous” consequences to selling clothes on vinted. She said that as she was now 25 and has continued to find sexualised images of herself online,, the risk did not end at 18.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a vinted spokesperson said: “we have zero tolerance for harmful or explicit content and use a combination of dedicated moderation teams and detection tools to spot and remove activity that breaks our rules. When we identify inappropriate behaviour, we take action, up to a permanent ban or reporting to the relevant authorities. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, an ebay spokesperson said: “we have clear policies and safeguards to protect our community, including encouraging people to keep conversations on ebay, avoid sharing personal contact details and report any suspicious or inappropriate behaviour. Where we or our customers identify policy violations, we take appropriate action. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa depop said: “using someone’s images without their permission is a violation of our terms of service, which explicitly prohibits users from using or sharing another user’s content without their consent, whether on depop or elsewhere. We take the safety of our community extremely seriously and we have robust policies, controls and processes in place to protect our users. ”.

#396. EU leaders gather for first ever AI summit

The summit comes as worries about the artificial intelligence's global impact mount and Europe seeks a role in its development and regulation.

Berdasarkan laporan, european union leaders are meeting in dublin on friday at the first ever summit on artificial intelligence (ai). The meeting comes at a critical moment, as the bloc seeks a unified policy on the rapidly evolving technology.

"Given the rapid pace of AI development, ​I ‌believe that a first dedicated discussion, at leaders' level, is now needed on the opportunities presented by AI, as well as on its transformative effect on our economies and societies," European Council ‌President Antonio Costa wrote in a letter to EU leaders last week.

The meeting is taking place in Dublin's Convention Center, which was also the meting place of the European Political Community summit this week.

French AI company Mistral's CEO Arthur Mensch, as well as Nobel-prize winner and researcher Geoffrey Hinton, widely known as the "godfather of AI," are expected to speak to EU leaders at the summit.

The summit will take place a time of mounting worries about the emerging technology, which promises to transform ‌industries, labor markets and societies.

It also comes in the wake of a series of incidents involving rogue AI agents in recent months and the wider discussion about how the technology could harm humanity.

Diungkapkan bahwa tech leaders behind the technology have also fallen under scrutiny. As recently as this week,Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was forced to resign after it was revealed that he had been in a relationship with a Chinese spy and a direct report in his company.

During the summit, a discussion about where Europe fits in within the AI movement is expected.

Leaders face questions on how to unlock AI's potential, how to catch up with China and the United States in the race for the technology, but also how to protect against the risks it poses to individuals and businesses.

Berdasarkan laporan, the governments of estonia and finland wrote in a letter ahead of the summit that europe must "establish eu-level arrangements for responding to serious ai incidents," calling for "developing advanced ai and governing it responsibly. ".

Meanwhile, Mistral has pushed back on calls to slow down AI development, urging Europe to push ahead.

#398. Why midterm vote-counting is taking so long in America's largest state

📅 13 Nov 2026

Why midterm vote-counting is taking so long in America's largest state

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqly4ljvr4pjo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

The results of the Alaska midterm elections might not be known until 18 November.

For the last few weeks, in addition to its usual payload of passengers, medicine, and supplies, Alaska Seaplanes has carried some unique cargo: midterm election ballots.

The regional airline is a piece of a complex logistical puzzle that sees Alaskans' ballots cast by mail and in person carried across the vast expanse of America's largest state, which is primarily connected by water and air rather than roads.

This considerable task explains why, a week after most US states knew their results in the midterms - in which the Democrats won back both chambers of Congress from the Republicans - Alaskans are still waiting for the Senate race to be called.

The victor in this close contest between the incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan and his Democratic challenger, former congresswoman Mary Peltola, could remain unknown until 18 November, when officials expect to have counted all eligible ballots.

"We do feel a sense of pride of making sure we do the job right - the really complicated job of getting all these ballots across thousands of miles in Alaska," Andy Kline, the marketing director of Alaska Seaplanes, which serves the south-eastern part of the state, told the BBC.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we feel like we're part of the last leg of that journey of those ballots. ".

An Alaska Seaplanes aircraft similar to the ones that transport ballots, along with other cargo and mail, during elections.

Some precincts in Alaska are able to communicate their initial results to centralised election offices on election night, allowing state officials and news outlets to report some preliminary vote tallies.

But it takes some time for the full picture of how people have voted to emerge.

As well as having the logistical challenge of counting votes from across a state more than six times the size of the UK, there is a delay waiting for mail ballots to arrive, says Charles Stewart, an election expert at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

These ballots can arrive up to 10 days later, or 15 days for overseas voters, if postmarked by election day.

Stewart said that election officials had "chosen to err on the side of getting it right rather than a rush to report the second and third tranches of ballots that get counted".

Regardless of whether ballots were cast in person or by mail, all of them eventually wind up in the state capital of Juneau â which is only reachable by plane or boat â for scanning and counting.

While more urban districts can get their materials on a plane late on election night, it takes longer for smaller or more remote parts of Alaska.

In some places, "you get someone who's basically running the election for their family and their neighbours because it's such a small village", says Scott Kendall, an election lawyer who previously worked on two campaigns for Alaska's other Republican senator, Lisa Murkowski.

In these smaller areas, ballots are sealed up in special envelopes or containers and sent it through the mail - which is where companies like Alaska Seaplanes comes in.

Ballots are put on the planes and sent to Juneau, where they then get dropped at the post office and delivered.

"It's part of our daily routine, just another couple of boxes," Kline said.

Former congresswoman Mary Peltola is the Democratic candidate.

Once all the in-person and absentee mail ballots reach Juneau, election officials will complete their review.

If no candidate gets more than 50% of the vote in the first round, officials will quickly use ranked-choice voting to re-allocate votes from the lowest-scoring candidates to their voters' second choices.

Then Alaska will finally declare a winner for its Senate race, as well as contests for governor and US House of Representatives.

Berdasarkan laporan, adding to the suspense of who will win the senate race is the question of whether another republican candidate called dan sullivan, who was allegedly recruited by democratic operatives, would affect the outcome. Results released so far suggest a low probability.

Berdasarkan laporan, this week, president donald trump alleged alaska's senate election had been "rigged" due to the second dan's involvement. His administration is appealing its rejected lawsuit to halt certification of the election over the issue, which a lower court dismissed.

US Senator Dan Sullivan of Alaska is one of two men with the same name who were on the ballot.

Meanwhile, a judge has denied an attempt by Peltola's campaign to get information about how many absentee ballots election officials rejected, as well as information about those voters.

The state argued it had no obligation to share this data, and doing so would violate voter privacy.

While the result of the election is of the greatest importance to many, for people like Kline the process is also key.

"We're all citizens," he said of himself and his colleagues.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we all feel like we have skin in the game to make sure that our elections are accurate and timely. ".

#401. Whatever happened to the $300,000 diamond that went missing in F1 crash?

📅 13 Nov 2026

Whatever happened to the $300,000 diamond that went missing in F1 crash?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/articles/c60735md0jrpo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Where were you between the hours of 1pm and 3pm on 23 May 2004?.

If you were in Monaco, consider yourself a suspect - or at least a witness - in Formula 1's biggest unsolved mystery.

A $300,000 diamond was last seen stuck to the front of an F1 car before it crashed on the first lap of the Grand Prix and it still has not been found 22 years later.

Did someone pick it up? Was it swept up with all the debris? Did it slip down a drain? Was it even a real diamond?.

Berdasarkan laporan, the reason why a 1. 4 carat diamond was attached to the most delicate part of a car that reaches 200mph in a race was straightforward: publicity.

Jaguar Racing's results on the track had been mediocre at best since becoming an F1 team in 2000 and by 2004 its parent company Ford had decided it would be pulling them out of the sport.

"My job flipped from primarily running the team to primarily selling the team and finding a new owner or they would shut it down," former team principal Tony Purnell tells BBC Sport.

Berdasarkan laporan, "it was probably the worst year of my life. Particularly because for the first few months I was sworn to secrecy. ".

His team needed some good PR to divert attention away from performance and improve its appeal.

They had enjoyed a successful promotional weekend in Silverstone the previous season thanks to a tie-up with Terminator 3 and so director of communications Nav Sidhu was looking to recreate the magic with another bit of help from a movie.

"I'd heard on the grapevine, around about the winter of 2003, that they were making Ocean's Twelve and we discovered that they were shooting some of the scenes in Monte Carlo," Sidhu says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "one thing led to another and before you knew it, we had agreed [a deal] with george clooney, brad pitt and matt damon. ".

Sidhu had arranged with legendary Hollywood producer Jerry Weintraub to have the film's branding and stars take over the team for the Monaco weekend.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the film plot centred on an audacious theft of a diamond-encrusted faberge egg. Sidhu decided he wanted some sparkle on his cars too at the most glamorous race in the F1 calendar.

Sidhu negotiated with diamond company Steinmetz that the two Jaguar cars would have gems - which would today be worth about $1m in total - attached to them.

What happened next, though, was not part of the script.

There was huge media interest in the appearance of the Hollywood stars.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while the champagne corks were popping on nearby mega yachts in the principality, the diamonds were being hand-delivered into the garages. There were two that would be mounted on to the car and a larger gem just for the photos.

Diungkapkan bahwa the diamonds for the cars were encased by steel and fixed to the nose cones. One on experienced driver Mark Webber's car and one on rookie Christian Klien's.

Sebagaimana diketahui, webber was starting from 11th place in the grid and klien - in only his sixth race - was starting from 14th. They weren't expected to challenge for the podium, but they were expected to bring the diamonds back.

Jaguar were given two different types of diamond for the weekend - one for promotional purposes (on the left) and one to be welded into the cars (on the right).

Monaco's street circuit is demanding, with narrow roads, tight turns and a tunnel.

Overtaking is difficult and crashes are common - as Klien soon found out.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in a chaotic first lap, the austrian made contact with one of the jordan cars exiting the mirabeau corner. This damaged the front of his car - where the diamond was - and led to a slow collision with the barriers at the famous Loews hairpin.

Klien climbed out unhurt but the front of the car was crumpled.

It was not long before Sidhu had the diamond company on the phone asking if they would get their diamond back.

"I can't remember what I answered, but it certainly wasn't 'yes'," he says.

He couldn't even get on to the track to have a look as the race had another 76 laps to go and only then would the car - which had been lifted off the track by a crane and left behind the barriers - return to the garage.

"I was consumed with getting to that spot as quickly as I possibly could," Sidhu says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "that hour and a half waiting for the race toâ¯finish felt like a day and a half, every single lap was just like pulling teeth. ".

By the time he had the chance to have a look, there was no sign of the diamond.

Sidhu completely denies the rumours of a fake diamond.

"I've learned that any diamond company is not going to go out there, particularly in the public domain, and use fake diamonds because clearly there's a high risk of being caught," he says.

"Had we used a fake diamond in that car and what took place took place, then clearly the embarrassment and the disrepute it would bring Jaguar, and Formula 1 for that matter, was too high risk.

Diungkapkan bahwa "there's been loads of conspiracy theories about was it a real diamond or was christian told to crash his car and i think that's what's given the story its life - there's a mystery to this story and that mystery will always breed different theories. ".

Purnell backs up the legitimacy of the diamond, recalling a conversation he had with the managing director of the team, David Pitchforth.

"David said, 'Tony, it was definitely real because when they came to the office with it, I picked the diamond up, went to the window and scratched the window' because that's how to tell.

"Hearing that from Dave, I'm in no doubt it was the real thing that was put on the car.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "i don't know if one of our mechanics was switched on enough to make a fake,â¯but i don't think so. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i think somebody probably just picked it up, put it in their pocket and. they're probably smiling and thinking, 'it's in my drawer'," says Purnell.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "i do think also that a fairly large diamond zooming through at 100 miles an hour probably shattered. Somebody's got a little bit, somebody else has got another [little bit].

"Maybe, sadly, just some guy was sweeping up the road or one of those trucks with the brushes and it all went down the sewer.

Diungkapkan bahwa "it did occur to me that the ultimate thing would be if clooney, pitt and damon had contrived to steal it because it was so in line with ocean's eleven. But that was a fantasy too far. ".

There would have been hundreds, if not thousands, of people in the area because within an hour or so of the end of the race the circuit would have been returned to public roads.

Sidhu is pretty certain about what happened to the diamond: "Someone's picked it up.

"What people tend to do is, believe it or not, pick up bits of tyre rubber, you know, claim that as Michael Schumacher's front tyre rubber or whatever they can find.

"Somebody may have picked it up not having any idea it came off a car.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "there's a lot of diamonds in monte carlo. There's a lot of people walking around Monte Carlo with a lot of jewellery and a lot of stones.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "somebody dropped a diamond in monte carlo. Well, they're not going to miss that, are they? Probably not. ".

Sidhu says the cost of the damage to the car was more than the cost of the diamond, which reports at the time said was uninsured.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and points and a good result in the race were more valuable to the team and individuals than a diamond or the publicity a crash would bring. It was simply not worth crashing on purpose.

"For us, bringing two cars home, ideally in the points,â¯had far bigger commercial benefits to us in terms of constructors' points, broadcast money,â¯and more importantly, trying to retain our sponsors and trying to protect the integrity of theâ¯team," Sidhu explains.

Klien drove straight into the barriers right in front of the marshals so would not have had the chance to start looking for a diamond or picking it up even if he had wanted to.

"Christian didn't try and say all the brakes failed or anything like that, he's just said 'I made a rookie mistake'," says Purnell.

Berdasarkan laporan, "he was a young guy, first time, made a mistake, it happens. Doesn't usually happen with a $300,000 diamond flying into the crowd or wherever it went, but I'm sure Christian wasn't really aware of the diamond.

Diungkapkan bahwa "no amount of money would have got christian to do that [crash on purpose]. He wanted to make a success of what he was doing. ".

While events were unfolding, Purnell had not really been thinking about the diamond.

His main concern that day was that one of his drivers had crashed and the other also did not finish, and that this was not a good look in terms of pleasing current backers or attracting potential buyers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "when christian went into the wall and then later mark retired, my entire thinking was 'oh god. What am I going to say?' The chairman of HSBC [Jaguar's then sponsors] was there, Sir John Bond. Jackie [Stewart] was there.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it was all about 'how am i going to explain another bad performance? how am i going to say 'just stick with the plan? we know what we're doing, it will take time' because sponsors don't have time. They want success. ".

In the end, the missing diamond came to the rescue.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "no-one mentioned jarno trulli winning the grand prix, no-one asked how the jaguars did. No-one was interested that Mark Webber's car broke as well. It was, 'where's the diamond?'" says Purnell.

Diungkapkan bahwa "i remember talking to somebody in detroit saying, 'fantastic publicity over here, you know we never hear anything about formula 1 but it's on the newscasts, it's in the papers - fantastic'. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, asked if the diamond mystery had helped the eventual sale of the team to red bull six months later, he replies: "i think that helped quite a lot because it buzzed the jaguar team and showed that huge publicity was possible even if you weren't doing so well. ".

Red Bull went on to become hugely successful, winning eight drivers' championships and six constructors' championships since joining F1.

"You couldn't design a better PR weekend," says Purnell.

Even if it was not quite how it was planned and there is still the small matter of a missing diamond.

Senator Van Hollen says midterm results show Americans want change in Washington, and Democrats need new leadership to deliver that.

Good morning, and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Barely a week after sweeping to a stunning midterm victory, Democrats have found themselves facing an altogether different battle, one within their own ranks.

Diungkapkan bahwa maryland senator chris van hollen has launched a challenge to chuck schumer, of new york, for the senate’s top democratic leadership post. Announcing his decision during an interview with MS Now last night, Van Hollen argued that last week’s midterm election results showed Americans wanted a fundamental change in Washington, and that Democrats needed new leadership in order to deliver that.

double quotation markWe saw a huge outburst of democracy on election day – red states, blue states, purple states – and it wasn’t only a rejection of Donald Trump and his corruption, his wars and his cruelty, it was also about a call for a larger change, to take on a broken economic system that’s rigged in favour of the very wealthy against working people, and it’s fuelled by a corrupt political system.

Diungkapkan bahwa the call was to reject the status quo and to reject business as usual, and to do that, i think we need new leadership. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa his challenge came just days after democrats secured control of the senate, winning at least 55 seats in what has been a remarkable election cycle for the party. Winning the leadership contest requires a majority of the caucus, about 28 or 29 senators, with an election scheduled for next month.

The caucus votes behind closed doors by secret ballot, but Van Hollen told MS Now that he had the support of “more than 10” Democratic senators.

Sebagaimana diketahui, progressive heavyweight bernie sanders, an independent senator from vermont who caucuses with the democrats, has already publicly declared he will not support schumer, saying “the time is now for change”. Endorsing Van Hollen, Sanders said: “The American people voted for change. They want a Democratic Party that will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families. ”.

Donald Trump is in Washington today, and will stay in the capital throughout the weekend.

He’ll spend the day in closed-door meetings on Friday, but we’ll let you know if anything opens up and we hear from the president in person.

Will JD Vance run for president in 2028? It’s a question that seems to have two rather different answers, depending on which news outlet you read.

Drawing on interviews with about a dozen people close to the US vice-president, CNN reported that his path to the Republican nomination has become less certain following the political fallout from the Republicans’ disappointing midterm performance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one source said: “i wouldn’t be surprised by any decision he makes. ” The same source pointed out that, at 42, Vance has plenty of time to pursue the presidency in future, adding: “It just may not be his time. ”.

#405. New York is running out of room for its waste even with Statue of Liberty sized landfill

📅 13 Nov 2026

New York is running out of room for its waste even with Statue of Liberty sized landfill

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/13/new-york-seneca-meadows-landfill

One company is proposing elongating the life of the dump, pungent smell and all, several more decades.

Berdasarkan laporan, as a visual representation of how new york is running out of places to put its waste, the largest active landfill in the state is a striking one. The hulking Seneca Meadows landfill is already the height of the Statue of Liberty and its operators are seeking to raise it even further, to the consternation of nearby residents.

The landfill, situated in the scenic Finger Lakes region in the northern reaches of New York state, has grown since the 1980s to now sprawl across 350 acres of deposited trash, mounded up to the height of around 300ft – roughly the same height of the Statue of Liberty.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “all around the lakes is pretty flat until you see this monster of a hill,” said mark pitifer, a marketing administrator at waterloo containers, a glass packaging company that sits next to the landfill and is dwarfed by its neighbor. “I mean it’s incredible, it’s like being in downtown New York City only instead of a building, it’s trash. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, locals in the nearby towns of waterloo and seneca falls, the latter famed as the birthplace of the women’s rights movement in the us, had hoped the bulging landfill would be closed when its permit expired last year. But the operator, Texas-based Waste Connections, has proposed elongating the life of the landfill for several more decades via 47 acres of newly lined disposal cells and adding another 70ft to the trash heap’s height.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as new york state authorities mull whether to grant this expansion, the landfill has become a central point of grievance over the pungent smell, water pollution and planet-heating pollution given off by the places we dump our rubbish. Seneca Meadows is now the largest source of methane, a potent greenhouse gas, in the state, according to a study last year based on researchers using aircraft measurements.

The operator, Waste Connections, did not respond to questions from the Guardian; it defends its environmental protections measures and record in statements on its website.

Berdasarkan laporan, the increasing size of landfills also raises uncomfortable questions about how much waste we produce and what to do with it. Seneca Meadows receives around 6,000 tons of trash each day from across New York, with 1,500 of those tons originating from New York City, which sends its rubbish to landfills hundreds of miles away that are rapidly filling up and are set to be completely full within the next 16 to 25 years.

If burning rubbish or casually dumping it into rivers and the ocean is too environmentally harmful, what is to be done with our waste beyond continually supersizing landfills to the point they become a major climate, as well as local, hazard?.

“We are at the precipice of a crisis,” said Emily Gallagher, a Democratic member of the New York state assembly who recently took a tour of the Seneca Meadows site and has convened a hearing on the state’s waste storage policies.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there is this huge mountain of trash that is off gassing almost 24 hours a day … contaminating the finger lakes, contaminating the groundwater,” she said of the site. “People we met in town are in really bad shape, we need to shut this expansion attempt down now. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, gallagher said intense lobbying and donations from interests aligned with the plastics and fossil fuels industries has stymied strict measures to reduce waste and enforce more recycling – she estimated 80% of the seneca meadows contents could be recycled. But she added there needed to be a broader societal reckoning with the tsunami of trash, much of it from cheap and disposal items, we create.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we say throwing away but there is no away,” said gallagher, whose district includes a part of new york city’s borough of brooklyn. “The problem is that it will take a culture change that people won’t want to do until it is forced in their faces. We used to have a much more circular economy, where people reused and rewashed everything, but we have been indoctrinated into a convenience culture, even if it then causes us more inconvenience. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dealing with trash is “gross problem”, gallagher acknowledged. “But we need a much deeper conversation about it rather than continuously pushing it to the side because it’s uncomfortable and it confronts our human desire for comfort and our laziness,” she added.

The municipal government of New York City has pointed to recent efforts to reduce its waste, such as the pickup and composting of organic matter, which makes up around a third of what is left as trash in the city.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, yet new york city residents still create around 12,000 tons of trash a day and it will need to go somewhere. The city does not send residential trash to Seneca Meadows – although some private contractors do – but will be sending it further and further from the city, which has not hosted its own waste for several decades.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “as capacity continues to shrink in the region, we will likely export trash to further locations,” said a spokesman for the city’s sanitation department. “Our commitment to rail export makes this much easier than trucking. ”.

Yvonne Taylor, co-founder of Seneca Lake Guardian environmental group, stressed she didn’t want other communities to suffer living near growing landfills like hers had.

Berdasarkan laporan, residents routinely text her to say that they have had to remove their children from the nearby school because the smell had sickened them, or of ruined outdoor birthday parties and other gatherings, she said. Pitifer, of Waterloo Containers, said the company has had to install filtration equipment to help employees deal with the overpowering stench of the landfill.

“We don’t need to use plastic grocery bags, we don’t need to use plastic toothbrushes, toothpaste, shampoo bottles, and laundry detergent bottles – all of those things can be packaged in other materials that don’t wind up in a landfill,” said Taylor.

Berdasarkan laporan, “so the solutions are out there. We just need the political capital to turn this around. ” In the meantime, though, the Seneca Meadows expansion must be halted, she said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we certainly don’t want to push this burden onto another community and say, “oh, we just don’t want it here. ” That’s not our philosophy at all,” Taylor said. You guys take it. “Our philosophy is that we need to start somewhere, and that somewhere is with Seneca Meadows. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the new york state department of environmental conservation and waste connections were both contacted for comment and did not respond. Waste Connections says on its website that it is “dedicated to the preservation and advancement of the environment” and has an “exemplary compliance record”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, its environmental protections include a “double composite liner” and a collection system for rainwater that has contacted waste. Landfill gas is captured and burned to generate electricity, it says, and there is ‘state of the art’ equipment and practices to capture odors which it says air monitoring data shows is effective. It says the gas is 50 per cent methane and it is collected and controlled, and the system is monitored to evaluate its effectiveness.
